Float64 norm/clip calculations diagnose the float32 optimizer approximately. No validation, model selection, inference export, room recording or board access.

interpretation: Shared global clipping has only a small classifier scaling effect in these samples; it does not explain the regression on its own. Scaled auxiliary encoder gradients vary widely and can exceed binary gradients, with most directions close to orthogonal and some opposed. This supports testing bounded encoder task balancing rather than assuming a clipping or frozen-head optimization failure.
limits: Only 16 original mixed batches at two fixed states. Gradient norms are not Adam update norms, a causal validation result, an independent sample or a wake-quality acceptance. No data/label/threshold/runtime changes, playback, microphone capture or board access.
